Episode 209. Temar's Seventh Tomb - Keitam's Painting (13)
When you reach the end of a Spirit Sword, it is not a swordsmanship, but a divine power.

That power is to take the life of a target whose willpower is weaker than the caster. Even if the absolute power possessed by the target surpasses the caster, the spirit cannot prevent itself from being cut.
And surely, among the mortals, Temar was the one who came closest to the end of the Spirit Sword.
Murakan also knew this well, so he was conscious of the Spirit Sword Cut from the beginning to the end.
Because he had personally seen Elona Zipil, who was clearly stronger than Temar, almost die due to a Spirit Sword Cut.
At that time, Elona Zipil showed a disintegrating figure, screaming as soon as the Spirit Sword Cut unfolded.
And the same was true of Murakan now.
[Aaaaah...!]
In a battle that lasted so long, Murakan, who never showed any signs of exhaustion or being pushed back, screamed in pain for the first time.
Whenever Murakan screamed and twisted his body, something like black smoke rose from his body, and the blade of Barisada drew that smoke.
As soon as the smoke touched the blade, Murakan felt the pain intensify. Instinctively, Murakan realized that Temar was cutting his soul.
It was not physically painful.
Things he tried hard to ignore, things he never wanted to remember again.
What was a recent event in the landscape for Murakan, and what was a thousand years ago for current Murakan. Whether then or now, it was a memory that was no different from disgust to Murakan.
Temar knew that perfectly. He said that in order to defeat Murakan, he had to directly hit his soul with the Spirit Sword.
Breaking his heart was a problem after that.
"It seems you do have something like emotions."
[Shu…t up…!]
"What day are you facing? The day when you slaughtered Dranaks and his Kamalga family? Or the day when you cruelly killed Violo who came to avenge you."
Grit…
As Temar was talking about the two, he gritted his teeth without realizing it. When he thought of those who had been wronged by Murakan, uncontrollable anger rose.
However, he had to suppress his emotions to prevent himself from falling into demonic rage again. If by any chance he fell into demonic rage again, he too would become a monster just like Murakan.

More than anything, it was a moment of revenge. If he messed up due to being drunk on anger, he felt that he wouldn't be able to forgive himself. He felt like he couldn't face his colleagues, knights, and people who trusted and depended on him, all who died to Murakan.

Therefore, even though he had a winning streak, Temar carefully deployed his Spirit Sword. As long as he was careful of the demonic rage, he would surely be able to cut off Murakan's breath, even if slowly.
As Temar said, Murakan was facing the day he killed Dranaks and Violo.
Dranaks had started using the name Runcondel in place of Kamal, but the members of the Kamalga family still regarded Dranaks as their leader.

His brother Kitan Kamal, who had just become the new family head, didn't feel uncomfortable about that. Rather, he was proud of his brother, and Dranaks also used to visit the southern part of Hufester and let off steam with his friends whenever he had time.
Kamal became one of the most important allied families of Runcondel, and all its members, like Dranaks, always aspired to be at the forefront of the battlefield.
Murakan enjoyed calling Dranaks and the Kamalga family a bunch of stick-in-the-muds tied together.
Until he decided to kill Dranaks and the entire Kamalga family, Murakan was very close to them.

"Murakan…! How could you do this! My brother trusted you more than me. If my brother had to choose between you and our Kamalga, he would have probably chosen you...he would have chosen you. He said it was for the world! How could you kill brother Dranaks."
Dark tears flowed from Murakan's eyes.

However, Temar's sword continued to wound his soul. As the black smoke was cut and scattered like paper, Murakan was buried in the painful memories that kept becoming clearer even with his eyes closed.
"Dranaks... What have I done to you."

"Dranaks… yes, he must have been strong enough to annoy you. But why did you slaughter the Kamalga family? You didn't even spare the children. What…grudge… was so deep towards Dranaks that fool... what wrong did Kamal's children do."
Violo, who came for revenge, choked and couldn't continue for a while.

"We were close. Even though we insulted each other and often hit each other, we never truly hated each other. At least, that's what Dranaks and our colleagues believed. They believed that if one day we fall while fighting Zipil, you will be the one to stay till the end for revenge, and to honor our spirits. If even you can't seek revenge, then at least you will remember us to the end…"
"Yes, Violo. I'll remember everyone. So, go to sleep now."

"No, you should forget us. Anyway, we won't be able to forget you even in death. We don't want to be remembered by you. Even as ghosts, we will curse you, and curse you again. The future of Soldelet, full of grudges, will also end up soaked in curse and blood, and will meet a dark end."
"[Violo...! I had no choice, I really had no choice!]
"I don't know what this situation is that you had no choice about, but whatever it is, it cannot justify what you've done. Even the Ziepel wouldn't have been so cruel."
Tears of bloody red flowed from the eyes of Temar. He was barely managing the thin gap between demonic possession and sanity.
"So, have you now come to view killing people as a mere amusement, Murakan. When people see your wings, they say that nothing remains there but ash. Because you don't even spare the children."
Frei Runkandel.

Even in the chaos, she strived to save people. She relieved the burden of those who suffered without hope, and wherever her gaze fell on the battlefield, there were always those who were the most difficult to survive.

"No, perhaps you were such a creature from the beginning. How suffocating must it have been to hide your hideous face all this time? But looking at us now... probably is enough compensation. There can be no greater reward than harming and trampling those who were deceived by you and gave everything."
Frei had bestowed countless mercies and loves in the world since she was born. But of them all, the only one she loved as a human being was Murakan.
She opposed Murakan much more fiercely than she had Dranaks and Violo who died before her.
She didn't end it in one battle, she fled somehow when cornered, promising a next time. Some days, she had a revelation just before dying and survived.
But it didn't last long. In the end, Frei met death in Murakan's Black Scythe.
"What I'm going through now... all... you... the manipulation of Ziepel... say it's true..."
Murakan, transformed into a human, sat down and wept with a weary voice. A thousand years ago, Murakan, and now, Murakan, crying and suffering were all he could do.
Before he knew it, Temar had almost cut off all the black smoke between him and Murakan. Now, if he took a few more steps, he could stab Murakan's heart.
Jin and the Ten Knights held their breath as if they were not observers but were actually standing right next to them.

Looking at the circumstances revealed so far, Murakan was clearly a traitor, and it was true that he had killed the Ten Knights. It was all Murakan's doing to massacre innocent people and make the whole of Hupester tremble with fear.
Despite this.

Jin and the Ten Knights, for some reason, were cheering for Murakan a thousand years ago. They hoped he would not fall like this, and they hoped he would not be stabbed by Temar as planned and fall into a long sleep."

"They were certain that there must be some reason for Murakan. They didn't know whether it could be justified as Temar said, but they couldn't imagine that Murakan would have done those things without reason.
The aura that formed the void space was all focused on Soul Slash.
The landscape that appeared as the darkness cleared was a vast and desolate land that looked like a gray desert. Not a trace of life could be found.

"Murakan, your memories have been transmitted to me through the sword. Dranaks, Violo, Frei. Comrades I sent off in vain without even a greeting, my friends. Even if I stab you a thousand, ten thousand times, the pain of losing them will not disappear. Their suffering will not be erased."
Thunk...!
Barisada plunged into Murakan's chest. The heart, weakened by the transformation, was pierced. It would have been the same even if it were the strongest heart in its original form.
Murakan showed no sign of feeling any pain.
"That's right, it should be..."
"When I twist my sword, you will disappear. It's frustrating that I can't cause you more pain and have to end it like this. I will ask one last question... Why did you do it?"
The hand of Temar holding the sword was trembling. The eyes on the dried tear marks were empty.
"What on earth is this situation you had no choice about? You committed these acts for the future a thousand years later? What does this terrible betrayal, this massacre have to do with it?"
"I don't know anything about... the future a thousand years later. I don't know anything about the truth of the world that you learned through the witch."
"Then why?"
Murakan slowly raised his head to look up at Temar.
"Temar, do you know... where we are now?"
"It's where you're going to die."

"Temar... here, this is. It may look like a land of death where nothing remains but ash... but once it was called Idal. It's the kingdom of Idal that Padlur ruled, which he loved more than his life..."
And Temar, you made Idal what it is now.
Continuing his words, Murakan grabbed the blade of Barisada with both hands.

"That's why I can't die now... even though I want to die like crazy. Temar. I'm sorry, before you commit more horrible acts, before you get more broken, before enemies use you more. I have to stop. Because I am, your guardian dragon."
